name: Milan
intro: Italy's design and fashion capital: a marble cathedral you can walk on, Leonardo's Last Supper, a castle park and canal-side evenings. A compact centre with a fast metro, and lakes an hour away.

transit.card: Contactless bank card or 90-minute urban ticket
transit.note: Tap the same card in and out on the metro; trams are a nice way to see the city.

sources: Written from general knowledge for the MVP; needs a human review before launch

areas.name: Duomo & Galleria
areas.blurb: The cathedral, the glass-roofed arcade and La Scala.

areas.name: Brera
areas.blurb: Art gallery, botanical garden and cobbled lanes.

areas.name: Castello Sforzesco & Sempione
areas.blurb: The castle and the city's big park.

areas.name: Last Supper & Sant'Ambrogio
areas.blurb: Leonardo's mural and the science museum.

areas.name: Navigli canals
areas.blurb: Canal-side cafés and the evening aperitivo.

areas.name: Porta Nuova
areas.blurb: Skyscrapers, the Vertical Forest and a new park.

areas.name: Porta Venezia gardens
areas.blurb: Natural history museum and public gardens.

areas.name: San Siro
areas.blurb: The football stadium in the west.

pois.name: Milan Cathedral (Duomo)
pois.why: A Gothic marble cathedral with 3,400 statues, built over six centuries.
pois.kid: Find the statue of St Bartholomew wearing his own skin like a cape.
pois.tip: Shoulders and knees covered; a combined ticket includes the terraces.

pois.name: Duomo rooftop terraces
pois.why: Walk among the spires on the cathedral roof, with Alps views on clear days.
pois.kid: Look for the golden Madonnina statue on the tallest spire.
pois.tip: The lift ticket costs more; the stairs are 250 steps.

pois.name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
pois.why: A glass-domed 19th-century shopping arcade, Milan's 'living room'.
pois.kid: Spin on your heel on the bull mosaic in the floor for good luck.

pois.name: La Scala Theatre Museum
pois.why: The opera house museum, with a peek into the auditorium when there's no rehearsal.

pois.name: San Bernardino alle Ossa
pois.why: A small church whose chapel walls are decorated with human bones.
pois.kid: Spooky but fascinating for older kids.

pois.name: Palazzo Reale
pois.why: The royal palace next to the Duomo, used for big temporary exhibitions.
pois.tip: Check what's on; tickets vary by exhibition.

pois.name: The Last Supper (Santa Maria delle Grazie)
pois.why: Leonardo da Vinci's mural, seen in a 15-minute timed visit.
pois.kid: Find the knocked-over salt cellar near Judas's elbow.
pois.tip: Tickets go on sale in batches and sell out fast; book as early as you can.

pois.name: Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio
pois.why: A 4th-century church with a calm brick courtyard and golden mosaics.

pois.name: Leonardo da Vinci Science Museum
pois.why: Italy's biggest science museum: Leonardo's machines, trains, a ship and a real submarine.
pois.kid: Visit the Enrico Toti submarine (separate timed tour).
pois.tip: Book the submarine tour when you arrive.

pois.name: Castello Sforzesco
pois.why: The Sforza family's brick castle, with free courtyards and museums inside.
pois.kid: Walk around the old moat and find the drawbridge.
pois.tip: The museums are closed on Mondays.

pois.name: Parco Sempione
pois.why: The city's central park behind the castle, with a pond and playgrounds.

pois.name: Arco della Pace
pois.why: Napoleon-era triumphal arch at the end of the park.

pois.name: Torre Branca
pois.why: A 108 m steel tower in the park with a lift to the top.
pois.tip: Opening hours are limited and weather-dependent.

pois.name: Pinacoteca di Brera
pois.why: Italy's great paintings from Mantegna to Caravaggio, in a historic palace.
pois.kid: Find the 'Dead Christ' painted from his feet up.

pois.name: Brera lanes
pois.why: Cobbled streets of galleries, cafés and fortune tellers.

pois.name: Brera Botanical Garden
pois.why: A small, free walled garden hidden behind the Brera gallery.

pois.name: Darsena
pois.why: The old harbour basin where the canals meet, now a waterside promenade.

pois.name: Naviglio Grande
pois.why: The canal lined with cafés, small shops and the famous evening aperitivo.
pois.kid: Look for the narrow 'Vicolo dei Lavandai', where people once washed clothes in the canal.
pois.tip: Best from late afternoon; a big antiques market runs on the last Sunday of the month.

pois.name: Bosco Verticale
pois.why: Two apartment towers covered in about 900 trees.

pois.name: Piazza Gae Aulenti
pois.why: A raised modern square with fountains kids run through in summer.

pois.name: Biblioteca degli Alberi park
pois.why: A new park of tree circles and meadows beside the skyscrapers.

pois.name: Natural History Museum
pois.why: Dinosaur skeletons, minerals and animal dioramas in a neo-Gothic building.
pois.kid: Count the dinosaur skeletons in the dinosaur hall.

pois.name: Giardini Indro Montanelli
pois.why: Old public gardens with ponds and playgrounds, next to the natural history museum.

pois.name: San Siro stadium tour
pois.why: Tour of the stadium shared by AC Milan and Inter, with a museum.

pois.name: Luini panzerotti
pois.why: A tiny bakery by the Duomo famous for fried dough pockets filled with tomato and mozzarella.
pois.tip: The queue moves fast; eat standing outside.

pois.name: Eataly Milano Smeraldo
pois.why: A big Italian food hall in an old theatre, with counters for pizza and pasta.

pois.name: Navigli trattorias
pois.why: Canal-side trattorias; try risotto alla milanese or cotoletta.

pois.name: Brera cafés
pois.why: Small cafés and trattorias in the lanes of Brera.

pois.name: Corso Magenta cafés
pois.why: Old pastry shops and cafés near the Last Supper.

dayTrips.name: Lake Como (Como town)
dayTrips.from: Trenord train from Milano Cadorna or Milano Centrale
dayTrips.why: Lake Como's main town: lakefront, ferries and a funicular up to Brunate.
dayTrips.tip: Ferries to Bellagio take longer than you think; check the return times.

dayTrips.name: Bergamo Città Alta
dayTrips.from: Train from Milano Centrale or Porta Garibaldi, then the funicular
dayTrips.why: A walled upper town of piazzas and churches above the modern city.

dayTrips.name: Varenna & Bellagio
dayTrips.from: Train from Milano Centrale to Varenna-Esino, then ferries
dayTrips.why: Pastel villages on Lake Como linked by short ferry hops.

dayTrips.name: Stresa & Borromean Islands
dayTrips.from: Train from Milano Centrale to Stresa, then boats
dayTrips.why: Lake Maggiore palaces and gardens with white peacocks.
dayTrips.tip: The island palaces open from spring to autumn.

dayTrips.name: Verona
dayTrips.why: Roman arena, Juliet's balcony and riverside streets.

tips.title: Getting around
tips.text: Tap a contactless bank card at the metro gates (in and out); fares are capped for the day. Trams and buses also accept contactless.

tips.title: Book ahead
tips.text: The Last Supper sells out weeks ahead: book on the official site as soon as tickets for your dates are released. The Duomo terraces also sell timed tickets.

tips.title: Dress code
tips.text: Cover shoulders and knees in the Duomo and churches.

tips.title: Aperitivo
tips.text: From about 18:00, bars along the Navigli serve a drink with a plate of snacks: an easy early dinner for families.

tips.title: Safety
tips.text: Watch for bracelet sellers and pickpockets around the Duomo and the Galleria. Emergency number: 112.
